idiom_name: Azure Service Bus sessions (SessionId + a session receiver); Channel<T> in-process
implementation_notes: The dominant .NET messaging service implements the group directly: Azure Service Bus sessions give exclusive, ordered handling of unbounded sequences of related messages - set the SessionId on each message, receive with a session receiver (AcceptSessionAsync / ServiceBusSessionReceiver), and the broker pins a session to one receiver while different sessions run concurrently, with session state covering receiver restarts. In-process, Channel.CreateBounded gives FIFO ordering with back-pressure, which replaces the sequence-number structure entirely while both ends share the process. The hand-rolled header plus buffer is needed only on transports that offer neither sessions nor ordering.
pitfalls: Sessions must be enabled on the queue or subscription and exist only on the Standard and Premium tiers; without a session id the queue gives no ordering guarantee.
A session receiver holds an exclusive lock: failing to close or dispose it blocks the session until the lock expires.
Channel<T> ordering is worthless across processes; do not use an in-process channel as a substitute for broker-level grouping.
